mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays elevated relative to its prior four-week level, commuting-linked discretionary trips convert into higher retail visits within four weeks, lifting RETAIL_REC above the recent average.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES remaining above its last-four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in RESIDENTIAL time indicates substitution away from outside trips, and that shift suppresses discretionary retail demand within one week and persists through four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 10% and stays there for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains above the stated threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS spikes while TRANSIT remains depressed, leisure demand is diverted toward outdoor substitutes rather than shopping centers, pushing RETAIL_REC down over the next two to four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 15 points from its prior week while TRANSIT stays below -25
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next 14 to 28 days after a PARKS surge occurs without a concurrent TRANSIT rebound.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT remains deeply negative, access friction to shopping districts persists and retail activity stays below baseline over the next four weeks; once transit recovers, the drag should fade.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -30 for 3 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves above its recent four-week mean while TRANSIT stays below -30 for the full trigger window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in PARKS and rise in GROCERY_PHARM signals a shift toward necessary, low-discretion trips; that mix reduces broader shopping visits and lowers RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days even though PARKS falls and GROCERY_PHARM rises relative to their recent averages.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rebound in PARKS after a prior trough reflects warmer-weather outdoor substitution that eventually competes with indoor retail, so RETAIL_REC is lower over the next four weeks than over the last four.
candidate_trigger: PARKS reverses from negative to positive week-on-week and stays above 0 for 2 weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -7.1 at t-0w after 36.3 at t-2w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite PARKS holding above zero for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both recover together, commuting density and foot traffic to commercial zones increase, generating a higher RETAIL_REC within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by at least 10 points and TRANSIT improves by at least 5 points within one week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its prior four-week mean after simultaneous improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent lift in GROCERY_PHARM combined with weak WORKPLACES indicates consumers are concentrating trips on essentials and avoiding discretionary venues, which keeps retail-and-recreation mobility below its recent level over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above 0 while WORKPLACES stays below -20 for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises within the next 7 to 14 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated and WORKPLACES remains suppressed.
